title: The Great Bank Consolidation Begins
text:
The Great Bank Consolidation Begins

Xiaoxi Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 24 Aug 2026

Financial regulators have for years vowed to “merge and reorganize” China’s thousands of small banks, many of which are in poor financial health. And for years, they achieved no progress. But that began to change in 2025, after top leader Xi Jinping ordered a reduction in the number of small banks and local governments became more willing to accept the need for mergers. With no official explanation and little media coverage, a major banking consolidation is now underway: the number of banks is falling sharply as officials orchestrate mass mergers of hundreds of financial institutions.The consolidation has so far concentrated on tiny village banks, and has made no discernible impact on the financial sector or economic growth. But the focus is likely to soon turn to the somewhat larger rural and city commercial banks. That will have more profound ramifications, as local governments use such banks to finance their off-balance-sheet spending. Consolidating these small banks would remove a key financial lever from the hands of many local authorities, constraining their ability to borrow and further re-centralizing control of the financial system.
